title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for liver metastasis.

HPI
Pt is a 61y/o female with hx of cancer of the right breast. Primary tumor was surgically removed and treated several years ago. Treatment for primary site is complete with no evidence of local recurrence at the original site. Pt now presents for management of liver metastases. Pt reports stable symptoms but seeks evaluation of hepatic involvement.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10mg QD
Atorvastatin 20mg QD

Exam
Gen: Well-appearing, alert, oriented x3.
Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 72, RR 16, Temp 98.6F, SpO2 98% RA.
Heart: RRR, regular rhythm, no murmurs.
Lungs: CTAB.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no hepatomegaly.
Skin: No new lesions noted.

Assessment
1. Liver metastases secondary to previous right breast carcinoma.
2. History of cancer of the right breast, stable.

Plan
1. Continue monitoring of liver metastases.
2. Order follow-up imaging to assess liver status.
3. Routine surveillance.

Electronically signed,
K. Nguyen, DO
05/14/2026
explanations: The right female breast cancer was excised or eradicated, no treatment is directed to it and there is no evidence of it: personal history Z85.3 (no HCC). Any metastasis is still coded as a current secondary malignancy.
Liver metastases: C78.7, secondary malignant neoplasm of liver (HCC 17).

distractors.why: Treatment ended and there is no evidence of the primary: code personal history (Z85), not active cancer.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in the liver, not bone.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Lung/Liver/Brain/and Other Organs; Acute Myeloid Leukemia Except Promyelocytic
